# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why4: An open box for up to four lines plus 'I'm not sure' as the only chip fits a benefit list, and that chip is the right way out.
screens.why5: Keel added nothing but the frame, so my two benefits stand exactly as I typed them.
screens.why7: The box asks for 1 to 4 benefits, one per line, each up to 9 words, naming what changes against today's way, with 'I'm not sure' as the founder's escape, which is the card's shape; my two rows fit it.

screens.why1: Right after I typed what it does better, Keel shows my benefits back as rows to check, which is exactly when I'd want to confirm them.
screens.why2: Hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew are how supers and I talk; nothing here needs a second read.
screens.why3: These are my own pitch, notes done during the walk instead of hours in the trailer and texting the crew their items, so I can judge them straight off.
screens.why4: Two distinct rows, one gain each, under 9 words, no overlap, and the 1-to-4 guidance and the keep-at-least-one rule fit an editable list.
screens.why5: Both rows are what I said (time saved after the walk, items out to the crew) with no number I didn't write, and the hard case of staying in the trailer typing logs is my problem in my words.
screens.why7: Both benefits are kept in order and joined with 'and', but the second reads oddly in the template ('would have given them action items to the crew'), and it is not flagged even though a super who types up within half an hour of the walk already gets items out the same day.
screens.instead: Keep the rows as 'Hours back at the end of the day' and 'Crew gets their action items the same day', and flag the second as something a fast same-day log may already deliver.

screens.why1: After saying how it fits and what it does better, asking what effort it asks of my supers is the obvious next thing before strangers judge it.
screens.why2: 'Setup, extra steps or learning' is plain to me, and the hint's limits (four, nine words) are clear on first read.
screens.why3: I know exactly what a super has to do differently with Fresco: call out the assignee while filming, then look over the notes before they go to the crew or Procore.
screens.why4: It's a free-text box with one escape chip, 'I'm not sure', which fits a founder who can't name the effort and correctly leaves the dimension out.
screens.why5: My two efforts come straight from how I describe Fresco (assignees named in the narration, notes checked before they're texted or pushed), and nothing is changed.
screens.why7: Both rows are efforts the super takes themselves, as base-form verb phrases within nine words, in 'they' voice, with no sign-off and no overlap with Compatibility's filming-on-the-walk or Purchase friction, so each can be answered Yes or No by a stranger.

screens.why1: Right after I said what they'd have to do to start, Keel shows back the efforts it drafted from my answer, which is where a check belongs in the solution step.
screens.why2: Both rows are in a super's own words: 'who owns each item' is how we talk about punch items and action items, and 'before they go out' is plain about notes going to the crew or into Procore.
screens.why3: Naming the owner while filming and checking the notes before sending are both things a superintendent does on their own walk and in their own log.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, each under 9 words and in a super's terms, with no overlap; the list is complete enough for me to pick one.
screens.why5: Naming the assignee as you film is exactly my mechanism ('needs replacement by Alex'), and reviewing the notes before they go out is the honest cost of that mechanism; nothing is changed from what I meant.
screens.why7: Each row is a base-form step the super takes themselves in the 'their' voice, neither repeats Compatibility's 'stop to film and talk' or Purchase friction's Procore check and security review, and either could be supported or refuted by Yes / Only if / Probably not / No with I can't tell apart.

screens.why1: After writing and checking the efforts, choosing the one most likely to stop a super is the obvious next step before the stranger's item.
screens.why2: Both rows are plain jobsite speech: saying who owns an item on a walk and checking notes before they go out to the crew are things every super does.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does on their own walk and in their own log, so they can answer from last week.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, both the super's own and both in their words, with no overlap and nothing missing that Compatibility doesn't already cover.
screens.why5: My narrated example ('needs replacement by Alex') and the 'assignees' I described are kept as 'name who owns each item as they film', and the pick matches mine, with no product name or buyer role leaking.
screens.why7: Each row is one base-form effort the super takes themselves, in their voice and the founder's order, with no repeat of Compatibility or Purchase friction; the belief can be supported or refuted on the four fixed answers, and the escape belongs on the stranger's item.

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out is the natural place to decide whether to collect emails, and as a founder who asked YC for intros to GCs I want warm leads from supers who say yes.
screens.why2: Short and plain, and the hint shows exactly the line respondents will see and where I'll find the yeses.
screens.why3: Whether I want pilot sign-ups is my own call about my own company, so I can answer it straight off.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers the choice completely, the two options are distinct, and no escape is needed for a founder's own decision.
screens.why5: My answer (Yes) is kept, and the respondent's line names nothing about Fresco, the price or the buyer roles, so nothing leaks.

screens.why1: Choosing who asks the questions belongs here, just before the link goes out to superintendents, and nothing earlier asked it.
screens.why2: Two names with a five-second sample and a plain note on cost and the text-message link; I can pick on first read.
screens.why3: It's my own study and my own credits, so it's a choice I can make myself.
screens.why4: Both voices are distinct and playable, but there are only two, both presented as women ('hear her'), with no option for a different voice that might suit a site audience of mostly men; the hint also says 'video' and 'voice' while what I locked was a face, so it's unclear what I'm picking.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product or buyer roles reaches the respondent; the screen only sets up how my questions are asked.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? (one line: the face and voice they'll see on video) -- Daphne ▶ 5 s / Saskia ▶ 5 s / a male voice ▶ 5 s

screens.why1: Choosing how the supers will take the study comes naturally right after picking who asks them and before sending, so it's clear why it's asked here.
screens.why2: AI interviewer, read and tap, and let them choose are plain to me, and each option says in one line what the super would do.
screens.why3: I know my supers: they're on their phones in the trailer at the end of the day, so I can judge whether they'd rather tap through or talk to a video.
screens.why4: The three options cover the real choices (AI voice, text, or either) without overlap, and a pick between formats needs no escape chip.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product or roles leaks here, and my pick of Read and tap is shown as I made it.

screens.why1: Once the interviews are set up, deciding who gets the links is the obvious last step before sending, and nothing earlier asked it.
screens.why2: Named people, a list from a search, or one link posted where supers already are are all plain on first read, though "Contacts page" is Keel's own word and I would only know it from the tool.
screens.why3: I know exactly who I can reach: the supers I've met driving around Napa and the South Bay, and the GCs I've been asking for introductions to.
screens.why4: The three ways to reach people are distinct and complete, and since this is a setup choice and not a question for respondents, no escape is needed.
screens.why5: My pick, sending each superintendent I know their own link, is kept as I made it, and nothing about my product or roles leaks to the people who will answer.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' is stated, but the line beside it names only Compatibility at 4 counted, and the 5 needed shows only down on the cards, so I have to piece together why from below.
screens.why_b2: Each card plainly says 4 counted against 5 needed, but the kicker says 7 answered and 4 counted without saying why the other 3 dropped out, so the 'over how many' takes a second look.
screens.why_b3: The three dimensions are mine and recognisable, but the beliefs are reworded: talking into the phone over the noise, a garbled relative-advantage sentence, and naming owners as they film. The statement also repeats 'notes with photos, assignees and due dates' twice.
screens.why_b4: Nothing says what to do: whether to get one more superintendent counted on each belief, or what the 4 who were counted lean toward.
screens.why_b5: It claims nothing beyond the 7 who answered, says plainly that each belief is short of the 5 it needs, and calls nothing held.
screens.instead: Too few to call on all three: 4 of 7 superintendents counted on each, 5 needed. Get one more counted answer per belief (here is why 3 weren't counted) before reading which way they lean.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know the answer and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 3 for and 1 against out of 5 answered, but 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 reads as if I need four yeses out of five, which blurs the 1-in-3 bar with the floor of 5, so I had to look twice.
screens.why_b3: It is my belief about talking into the phone over site noise, but it drops 'on commercial jobs' from my people and asks about the 'last daily log' instead of the site walk.
screens.why_b4: 'Ray's no is the one to ask about' gives me one person to call, but it never says I need one more counted answer or that 3 of 4 leans my way so far.
screens.why_b5: It is honest that the group is small and only a lean, but the question pins noise on site to 'your last daily log', which I write in the trailer, so the answers may not speak to the walk where people would actually film.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and they agree.
screens.why_b2: The chart plainly counts 3 better (all a lot) against 1 same over 4 people, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 mixes the floor of 5 with the 1-in-3 bar, so I had to look twice to see where the bar actually sits.
screens.why_b3: The belief line has both my benefits and my trailer-day clause, but the line 'You said hours back at the end of the day' drops 'action items to the crew the same day', and the asked line is cut off mid-phrase ('turns site-walk videos you talk').
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me that one more counted superintendent decides it, or that 3 of 4 saying a lot better is a lean my way.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (5 answered, 4 counted, Luis set aside as a guess), the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and nothing claims the belief held, though the count line's 'their last daily log' doesn't match the trailer day actually asked.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 needed counted. 3 said a lot better and 1 said no difference (Denise, whose log is done before she leaves the gate), so it leans your way on hours back and same-day action items; one more superintendent's answer decides it.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no answer yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The chart's counts are plain (1 yes, 2 only-if, 1 probably not, 0 no), but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' next to 'no more than 1 in 3 say probably not or no', plus a ghost cell and a marker at 4, made me stop and work out whether 4 of 5 is my bar, the floor or the count.
screens.why_b3: 'Adoption friction' and 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' are the effort I picked, though the bar line 'You said name who owns each item as they film' just echoes it awkwardly instead of saying what I'd set as the bar.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me to get one more superintendent's answer, and it doesn't flag that two of my three yeses hang on Fresco reliably catching the names I say on a noisy site, which is the actual product requirement here.
screens.why_b5: n=5 stays visible, Luis's guess is set aside and named, the conditional yeses are split out, and 'a small group: a lean, not a call' keeps it from overclaiming.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 counted, one short. Three would do it but two only if Fresco catches the names they say, so get one more super's answer and prove name pickup on a loud site.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on 'Too few to call' with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' right beside it, so I know both the verdict and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b3: The Compatibility line is the one I checked, word for word, but the Relative advantage belief reads as garbled ('their last day where they stayed in the trailer typing logs would have given them hours back'), though I can still recognise it.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more counted answer, but nothing says what this means for the idea, for example that the two who were against don't see the log as their problem.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible on every line, the low count is called 'Too few to call', and each group shows its 1 with no claim beyond it.
screens.why_b6: Ray says the log waits till morning when the deck can't, and Denise says she finishes hers on the tablet before the gate and that schedule and subs eat her day, which tells me the log isn't the top pain for some supers; I hadn't typed that.
screens.instead: Too few to call (4 of 5 needed); the two against both say the schedule and subs, not the log, eat their day, so ask more supers whether the log is really one of their two worst problems before trusting the solution lines.

screens.why1: As the very first screen it makes sense to check whether my jobs even run on something like Procore or ACC before asking anything else.
screens.why2: I'd answer it right away, but on site we'd just say Procore or ACC, and 'construction project management software' is a mouthful nobody on my job uses.
screens.why3: I know exactly what my jobs run on, so this is easy for me to answer.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it for a screener, and with no escape it fits a gate question.
screens.why5: Nothing about the product or the founder's plan shows up here, just a plain check on the software my jobs use.
screens.why6: It's short and one question, but 'construction project management software' is a long string to hear in one go, and 'I'll read 2 options' for a yes-or-no sounds stiff next to just 'Yes or no.'
screens.instead: Do any of the jobs you run now use Procore, ACC or similar project software? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my jobs run on project software, asking about this week's daily logs is the obvious next step and doesn't repeat anything.
screens.why2: Daily log and walk photos are my own words, and I can answer it the first time I hear it, though 'missing' could mean all the photos or just some.
screens.why3: I know whether I pushed a log out this week without the walk photos attached, because I'm the one who submits it.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it cleanly, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing about anybody's product, AI scribe or company terms comes through; it reads as a question about my log.
screens.why6: One short sentence ending in 'Yes or no' is easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: It is a single act in the window that can go either way: a super who got the photos in says No, and one who sent the log without them says Yes, so the share can hold or fail the founder's band with no escape.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you send in a daily log without the day's walk photos attached? Yes · No

screens.why1: After asking whether my jobs run on Procore and whether I've sent a daily log without my walk photos, showing me the idea before the idea questions is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Videos, assignees, Procore and ACC are all words I use, but nobody on a job site says 'scribe', and the card leans on it three times.
screens.why3: Walking the site, taking photos and video, handing out action items to the subs and getting it into Procore is my day, so I can picture this without guessing.
screens.why4: A card to read, with no options.
screens.why5: The last line just says it would be my scribe again instead of what it would do for me, like saving the hours I spend uploading photos and writing up the daily log, so the belief has drifted into repeating the name.
screens.why6: It says mostly fine, but 'turns site-walk videos you talk over into notes' is a mouthful heard once, and the scribe line at the end sounds like a repeat rather than a point.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an app that writes up your site walk for you. You take short videos on the walk and talk over them; it turns them into notes with photos, who's on it and when it's due, texts the crew their items, and sends it all to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe it would save you the hours you spend after the walk getting photos and notes into the daily log.

screens.why1: Right after the card about talking over walk videos, it's obvious they'd ask whether I could actually talk into my phone out there with saws and the pump truck running.
screens.why2: Plain words I'd use myself: phone, noise on site, talked into it.
screens.why3: I talk on the walk, not when I write the log at the trailer, so 'your last daily log' makes me work backwards to which walk it means and I'd partly guess.
screens.why4: Easily, most of the time, sometimes, no covers it; some days I can and some days the concrete crew drowns me out, and 'I can't tell' fits.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks past the idea card shown on purpose; the question is about my phone and the noise, in site words.
screens.why6: One short question and four short options I can hold, with the escape said last.
screens.why7: It asks an ability on one measure, could I have, with the ability four in order and 'I can't tell' apart; it can go for or against, since some sites are too loud.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have talked into your phone over the noise on site? Yes, easily · Yes, most of the time · Only sometimes · No · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the talking-over-noise question, asking whether Fresco would have beaten my last day stuck in the trailer is the obvious next thing to ask.
screens.why2: The trailer, uploading photos and typing daily logs are my words, but 'site-walk videos you talk' is cut off mid-phrase and I'd have to read it twice to work out it means talk over.
screens.why3: I've stayed in the trailer after the walk uploading photos to Procore and typing the log plenty of times, so I can answer from my own last one.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference and worse cover it without overlap, and 'I can't tell' fits as the way out.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks that the idea card didn't already show me, but the repeated description drops 'over into notes', so it no longer says what the card said Fresco does.
screens.why6: Heard once, the stem runs well past twenty words and the broken 'videos you talk, have done that' clause trips the ear, though the four options and the escape say fine.
screens.why7: The occasion is the day it cost me, not just any last log; the options are the fixed four on one better-or-not measure, two for and two against, so the belief can be backed or refuted; and 'I can't tell' is the only escape.
screens.instead: Think of the last day you stayed in the trailer uploading photos and typing the daily log. Would Fresco, an AI scribe that turns site-walk videos you talk over into notes, have done that better for you, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: After asking whether it would have beaten my trailer evenings, it makes sense to ask what extra I'd have to do on the walk to use it.
screens.why2: On a job 'owner' means the building owner, so 'who owns each item' makes me stop and work out that it means which sub or which of my guys has the ball on it.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day and know which sub is on each issue, so I can say whether I'd call it out while filming.
screens.why4: Yes, a real condition about it catching the sub names I say, probably not, and no are distinct and cover my true answer, with 'I can't tell' set apart.
screens.why5: Beyond the idea card I was shown on purpose, nothing of their plan leaks, and the step reads as a plain thing I'd do on a walk.
screens.why6: One short question and four short options I can hold, with the escape said last.
screens.why7: The step is my own new habit of use, the four options run on the one measure of whether I'd take that effort, two count for and two against, the condition is specific to this step, and 'I can't tell' is the one escape.
screens.instead: To use Fresco, you'd say which sub is responsible for each item as you film. Would you do that, or not? Yes · Only if it picks up the names I say · Probably not · No · I can't tell.
